dal-baati-churma.d: Balls of hard wheat dough baked then dipped in melted ghee, served with a mixed lentil dal and a sweet churma of pounded wheat with sugar and cardamom. Three textures, three temperatures, one Rajasthani platter.
s: Knead whole wheat flour, melted ghee and water into a firm dough, shape into thick balls.
Bake the balls 30 minutes at 180°C until firm and cracked, turning halfway.
Cook both lentils together with turmeric until tender, fry onion, tomato and cumin then mix into the dal.
Crumble a third of the baked balls, pound with sugar, cardamom and melted ghee for the churma.
Dip the remaining balls in melted ghee, serve the trio of dal, baati and churma on one platter.

dapanji.d: Chicken pieces simmered with potato and peppers in a sauce both spicy and lightly sweet, poured still steaming over wide hand-pulled fresh noodles, a Uyghur speciality of the Silk Road.
s: Knead flour, water and salt into a supple dough, rest 1 hour under oil, stretch into wide flat noodles.
Fry the chicken pieces with garlic, dried chillies, Sichuan pepper and star anise in oil.
Add potato in large chunks, soy and sugar, moisten and simmer 30 minutes.
Add the pepper strips for the last 10 minutes of cooking.
Cook the noodles in boiling water 3 minutes, drain and pour the chicken and its scalding sauce over the top.

yangzhou-fried-rice.d: Day-old rice, wok-fried grain by grain over high heat with ham, shrimp and peas, every grain meant to stay separate and coated in golden egg, never sticky. A classic born in the imperial kitchens of the Sui dynasty.
s: Use rice cooked the day before and well chilled, fluff with a fork to separate the grains.
Beat the eggs, scramble them quickly in the very hot wok, set aside in small pieces.
Fry shrimp and diced ham in oil until just cooked.
Add the rice, stir-fry over high heat, stirring constantly to separate the grains well, add peas and egg.
Season with soy sauce and sesame oil, scatter with chopped scallion and serve immediately, piping hot.

guilin-rice-noodles.d: Fresh rice noodles drowned in a pork and bone broth simmered for hours with spices unique to each stall, topped with marinated pork and peanuts, an unmissable breakfast dish in the karst streets of Guilin.
s: Boil the pork bones 5 minutes, rinse to remove the scum.
Return to cook with star anise and cinnamon in plenty of water, simmer 3 hours over very low heat.
Marinate and roast pork slices until well fragrant, slice thinly.
Warm the fresh rice noodles in boiling water a few seconds, drain and place in a bowl.
Pour the hot strained broth over, top with marinated pork, peanuts, pickled beans, scallion and a drizzle of chilli oil.

guobaorou.d: Thin pork slices coated in starch and fried twice until extra crisp, then quickly tossed in a translucent sweet-sour sauce, a northeastern Chinese speciality invented to please Russian diplomats in the early last century.
s: Slice the pork thin, flatten lightly.
Mix starch, egg and a little water into a thick batter, coat each slice.
Fry once for 2 minutes at 160°C, drain, then fry a second time at 190°C until very crisp.
Make a sauce by heating sugar, rice vinegar, soy and garlic until syrupy and translucent.
Pour the scalding sauce over the fried pork just before serving, tossing quickly to coat without softening it, scatter with coriander.

banh-mi.d: A baguette inherited from French colonisation, with light crumb and thin crust, split and filled with pâté, grilled pork, vinegar-pickled vegetables and fresh coriander — the most successful meeting of French bakery and Vietnamese cuisine.
s: Cut carrot and daikon radish into fine julienne, marinate 30 minutes in vinegar and sugar.
Marinate the thinly sliced pork in soy sauce, grill 3 minutes per side.
Split the baguette lengthwise without cutting all the way through, spread with pâté and mayonnaise.
Fill with grilled pork, drained pickled vegetables and cucumber slices.
Finish with a few sprigs of fresh coriander and serve at once, crisp.

bun-cha.d: Marinated pork patties grilled over charcoal until caramelised, dipped along with cold rice vermicelli and fresh herbs into a warm sweet-salty-tangy nuoc cham bowl, an emblematic lunchtime dish of Hanoi's sidewalks.
s: Mix minced pork with a little fish sauce, sugar and crushed garlic, shape into small flat patties.
Grill the patties over charcoal embers 4 minutes per side until caramelised.
Make the nuoc cham by mixing fish sauce, sugar, lime juice, warm water, minced garlic and chilli.
Cut the carrot into fine julienne, add it lightly marinated to the nuoc cham.
Serve the grilled patties floating in the warm nuoc cham, with cold rice vermicelli and fresh herbs on the side for dipping.

tom-yum-goong.d: A shrimp soup that is at once fiery, sour and fragrant, where lemongrass, galangal and kaffir lime leaves infuse a clear broth spiked with chilli and lime juice at the very last moment, to preserve its zing.
s: Shell the shrimp, reserving the heads and shells.
Fry the shells with lemongrass, galangal and kaffir lime leaves in a little oil, moisten with water and let infuse 15 minutes, strain.
Bring the strained broth to the boil, add mushrooms and tomato, cook 5 minutes.
Add the shelled shrimp, cook 3 minutes until they turn pink.
Off the heat, season with fish sauce, lime juice and crushed chilli, scatter with coriander and serve immediately.

som-tam.d: Grated green papaya pounded in a mortar with garlic, chilli, cherry tomato and long beans, dressed with fish sauce, lime and palm sugar, the clatter of the pestle against the wooden mortar setting the rhythm of Isan's streets.
s: Shred the green papaya into fine strips.
Pound garlic and chilli in a mortar, add the cut long beans and pound lightly to soften them.
Add the shredded papaya and halved cherry tomatoes, pound and mix without turning to purée.
Season with fish sauce, palm sugar and lime juice, pound again to blend the flavours well.
Scatter with crushed peanuts and dried shrimp, serve immediately, well chilled.

manti.d: Tiny dumplings stuffed with minced beef, so small that tradition holds you should fit forty on a single spoon, drowned under garlic yoghurt and a sizzling paprika oil poured at the table.
s: Knead flour, egg, water and salt into a very firm dough, rest 30 minutes.
Mix the minced beef with grated onion pressed to extract its juice, salt.
Roll the dough extremely thin, cut tiny 2 cm squares.
Fill each square with a dab of filling, pinch the four corners together to close.
Poach the mantı 10 minutes in boiling water, drain, top with garlic yoghurt and sizzling paprika butter poured hot at the table.

lahmacun.d: Dough stretched paper-thin, spread edge to edge with a raw paste of minced meat, tomato, pepper and spices, baked just a few minutes in a very hot oven, rolled around parsley and lemon to be eaten by hand.
s: Knead flour, water, yeast and salt into a supple dough, let rise 1 hour.
Blend raw minced meat, tomato, pepper, onion, garlic and paprika into a fine, even paste.
Divide the bread dough into balls, stretch each as thin as possible into an almost transparent disc.
Spread a thin layer of the meat paste to the edges of each disc.
Bake 6 to 8 minutes in a very hot 250°C oven, roll around fresh parsley and a squeeze of lemon before serving.

gado-gado.d: A composed salad of cooked and raw vegetables, tofu, tempeh and hard-boiled egg, drowned under a thick peanut sauce scented with kecap manis, Indonesia's sweet soy syrup. Its name literally means "mix-mix".
s: Separately cook cabbage, green beans, bean sprouts and potatoes by steaming until tender but still crisp.
Fry the tofu and tempeh in golden dice, hard-boil the eggs.
Dry-roast the peanuts, blend with garlic, chilli, kecap manis, lime juice and a little water into a thick sauce.
Arrange all the vegetables, tofu, tempeh, eggs and raw cucumber on a large platter.
Coat generously with the peanut sauce and serve at room temperature.

sate-ayam.d: Small cubes of marinated chicken threaded onto bamboo skewers, grilled over coconut shell embers until lightly caramelised, served with a thick peanut sauce and compressed rice, a speciality of Madura island famed for its street vendors.
s: Cut the chicken into small cubes, marinate with soy, crushed garlic and ground coriander for 30 minutes.
Thread the cubes onto bamboo skewers pre-soaked in water.
Grill over moderate embers 8 to 10 minutes, turning regularly, until lightly caramelised.
Dry-roast the peanuts, blend with kecap manis, chilli, lime juice and a little water for the sauce.
Serve the skewers coated with peanut sauce, with compressed rice cubes.

jambalaya.d: Rice simmered in a broth coloured by the Creole holy trinity — onion, celery, green pepper — with smoked andouille sausage and shrimp, heir to Spanish paellas and African pilafs brought together by centuries of Louisianan mixing.
s: Fry the sliced smoked sausage until it releases its fat, set aside.
In the same fat, sweat chopped onion, celery and green pepper until tender.
Add garlic, tomato, cayenne and bay leaf, fry 2 minutes, return the sausage.
Add the rice, moisten with chicken broth, cover and cook 20 minutes over low heat without stirring.
Add the shrimp for the last 5 minutes, mix gently and serve piping hot.

philly-cheesesteak.d: Thinly sliced beef griddled on a flat-top, mingled with softened onions and drowned in melted cheese, piled into a soft roll — a sandwich born in the 1930s whose version every local defends for their own neighbourhood.
s: Freeze the beef slightly to ease slicing, cut into very thin strips.
Melt the sliced onion in butter on a hot griddle until browned.
Add the beef, grill it quickly, chopping it with a spatula as it cooks.
Scatter the cheese over the hot meat, let it melt as you fold everything together.
Fill the split hoagie roll with this steaming mixture and serve immediately.

nashville-hot-chicken.d: Fried chicken with an extra-crisp coating, brushed straight from the fryer with a scorching paste of cayenne pepper and hot fat, served on a slice of white bread with pickles to soak up the fire.
s: Marinate the chicken pieces in buttermilk at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Drain, dredge in flour seasoned with salt and pepper, pressing well to adhere.
Fry at 175°C for 15 to 18 minutes until deep golden and crisp, turning halfway.
Mix cayenne, brown sugar, paprika and a little scalding frying oil into a thick paste.
Generously brush the still-hot chicken with this paste, serve on white bread with pickles.

kalua-pig-laulau.d: A whole pig buried for hours in an underground imu oven heated with volcanic stones, emerging smoky, salty and falling apart, served alongside laulau — pork and fish wrapped in steamed taro leaves — the centrepiece of the luau feast.
s: Rub the pork shoulder generously with sea salt and liquid smoke to mimic the imu flavour.
Wrap in banana leaves, bake at a low 190°C for 5 hours until it falls apart.
For the laulau, wrap pieces of pork and fish in several taro leaves, then in a banana leaf.
Steam the laulau parcels 3 hours until the taro leaves are meltingly soft and no longer irritating.
Shred the pork with a fork, serve with the laulau parcels opened at the table.

new-mexico-green-chile-stew.d: A pork and potato stew carried by Hatch green chiles, roasted until blackened then peeled by hand, whose smoky, earthy flavour sets New Mexican cooking apart from the rest of the American Southwest.
s: Roast the green chiles over an open flame or in the oven until the skin is fully blackened.
Seal them in a plastic bag 10 minutes then peel, seed and chop.
Brown the cubed pork with onion, garlic and cumin in a pot.
Add the chopped chiles, diced potato and broth, bring to the boil.
Simmer 45 minutes covered until the pork is tender, season with oregano and serve with tortillas.

cochinita-pibil.d: Pork marinated in achiote that dyes it deep red, wrapped in banana leaves and originally cooked in a buried pit oven called a pib, inherited from the Maya, emerging tender and fragrant with bitter citrus.
s: Dilute the achiote paste in sour orange juice and crushed garlic into a smooth marinade.
Coat the pork generously with this marinade, let rest at least 4 hours or overnight.
Wrap the marinated pork in banana leaves passed over a flame to soften them.
Bake the parcel 4 hours at 150°C until the meat shreds easily.
Shred the pork, serve with red onion pickled in vinegar and habanero, with tortillas.

mole-negro.d: An almost-black sauce blending chilhuacle chiles roasted to bitterness, chocolate, spices and dried fruit, reduced for hours into a complex paste that coats the chicken — the most elaborate of Oaxaca's seven moles.
s: Dry-roast the dried chiles until nearly black and brittle, soak in hot water.
Likewise roast almonds, raisins, sesame and a torn tortilla until browned.
Blend the drained chiles, roasted dried fruit, tomato and cinnamon with a little broth into a smooth paste.
Fry the paste in a pot 20 minutes, stirring constantly to prevent sticking, add the chocolate and remaining broth.
Simmer the chicken in this sauce 40 minutes until tender and the sauce is thick and glossy.

huachinango-veracruzana.d: A whole red snapper braised in a tomato sauce scattered with green olives, capers and sliced jalapeño peppers, a direct legacy of Spanish, Arab and Caribbean influences converging in Mexico's first colonial port.
s: Sweat chopped onion and garlic in olive oil until translucent.
Add crushed tomato and bay leaf, simmer 15 minutes until reduced.
Add green olives, capers and sliced jalapeño, simmer another 5 minutes.
Place the whole fish in the sauce, cover and cook 15 minutes, basting regularly.
Check the flesh flakes easily with a fork and serve the fish coated in its sauce.

feijao-tropeiro.d: Drained black beans then fried with cassava flour, bacon, sausage, collard greens and scrambled egg, a hearty dish born from the tropeiro mule drivers who crossed Minas Gerais with provisions that kept for weeks.
s: Boil the black beans until tender, drain reserving a little of their water.
Fry bacon and diced sausage until crisp, add onion and garlic.
Add the drained beans, mix over high heat a few minutes.
Gradually stir in the cassava flour, stirring to coat without lumps.
Add the shredded collard greens and separately scrambled egg, mix everything together and serve hot.

acaraje.d: Fritters of shelled black-eyed peas, ground and fried in red dendê palm oil until forming a golden crust, split open and filled with vatapá and dried shrimp, sold by white-robed baianas on Salvador's streets.
s: Soak the black-eyed peas overnight, rub between your hands to remove the skins.
Blend the shelled peas with onion and a little water into a smooth, airy paste.
Beat the paste vigorously with a spoon for several minutes to incorporate air.
Shape oval fritters with a spoon, fry in boiling dendê oil until golden.
Split each hot acarajé open, fill with vatapá and dried shrimp, serve immediately.

tacaca.d: A bright yellow broth of tucupi, bitter cassava juice fermented and boiled to remove its toxicity, thickened with jambu leaves that tingle and numb the tongue, garnished with dried shrimp, served scalding in cuias gourds hollowed from an Amazonian squash.
s: Boil the tucupi with crushed garlic for 30 minutes to fully purge its residual toxicity.
Separately blanch the jambu leaves in boiling water 5 minutes.
Dissolve a little cassava starch in cold water, stir into the boiling tucupi to lightly thicken it.
Rehydrate the dried shrimp in a little hot water.
Serve the scalding tucupi in a deep bowl with jambu leaves and dried shrimp arranged on top.

lomo-saltado.d: Beef quickly stir-fried in a wok with red onion and tomato, splashed with soy sauce, served with both fries and rice on the same plate — the most emblematic chifa dish born from the meeting of Cantonese immigrants and Andean cooking.
s: Cut the potatoes into fries, fry until golden and crisp, set aside.
Cut the beef into thick strips, sear very quickly in a scorching wok.
Add red onion and tomato in wedges, stir-fry another 2 minutes over maximum heat.
Deglaze with soy sauce and vinegar, shake the wok to coat well without releasing too much juice.
Add the fries at the end of cooking so they stay crisp, scatter with coriander and serve with white rice.

anticuchos.d: Skewers of beef heart marinated in aji panca chili paste, cumin and vinegar, grilled over embers until just caramelised outside while staying tender within, an Incan tradition kept alive on Peruvian street braziers.
s: Trim the beef heart, removing sinew and membrane, cut into even cubes.
Mix aji panca paste, vinegar, cumin and crushed garlic into a thick marinade.
Coat the heart cubes with this marinade, let rest at least 4 hours chilled.
Thread the cubes onto wooden skewers, brush with a little oil.
Grill over hot embers 3 to 4 minutes per side, basting with marinade, serve immediately piping hot.

empanadas-saltenas.d: Small pastry turnovers folded into a tight braided edge, stuffed with knife-chopped beef, hard-boiled egg, olive and cumin, baked in a wood oven, a speciality of northwestern Argentina where every province jealously claims its own recipe.
s: Knead flour, melted butter, warm water and salt into a supple dough, rest 30 minutes.
Fry the very finely chopped onion with cumin and paprika until soft, add the knife-chopped beef.
Moisten with a little broth to keep the filling juicy, let cool then stir in chopped hard-boiled egg and olives.
Roll out the dough, cut circles, fill with the mixture and close, pinching the edges into a tight braid.
Bake 20 minutes at 200°C until golden, serve hot.

ajiaco-bogotano.d: A chicken soup thickened by three varieties of Andean potato that break down at different speeds, scented with guasca, a local herb found nowhere else, served with sour cream, capers and half a corn cob.
s: Poach the whole chicken in the broth with onion and garlic 40 minutes until tender, shred the meat and reserve the broth.
Peel the three potato varieties, cut into pieces of different sizes according to how readily each breaks down.
Cook the potatoes in the broth 25 minutes, stirring, some dissolving to thicken the soup.
Add the shredded chicken and the corn cobs cut into chunks, simmer 10 minutes.
Add the guasca at the end of cooking, serve with sour cream, capers and a piece of corn per bowl.

civet-de-sanglier-corse.d: Wild boar hunted in the maquis, marinated several days in red wine and myrtle, simmered for hours until the sauce naturally thickens with blood, a winter hunting dish served with local chestnut polenta.
s: Cut the boar into large chunks, marinate 48 hours in red wine with myrtle berries, juniper, onion, carrot and bay leaf.
Drain the meat, reserving the marinade, brown it vigorously in a pot.
Add the vegetables from the marinade, moisten with the strained wine, simmer covered 2h30 over very low heat.
Check the sauce has naturally thickened and the meat pulls apart easily, adjust seasoning.
Make the chestnut polenta by stirring the flour into boiling salted water, serve the civet coated in its sauce with the polenta.

poulet-vallee-auge.d: A farmhouse chicken flambéed in calvados then simmered in a thick fresh cream sauce with softened apples, an emblematic dish of the Pays d'Auge where apple orchards, dairy cows and stills shape the landscape.
s: Brown the chicken pieces in butter until nicely coloured.
Warm the calvados, pour over the chicken and flambé off the heat.
Add the sliced onion and dry cider, simmer covered 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, fry the apple wedges in a little butter until tender and golden.
Stir the cream into the cooking juices, let thicken a few minutes, add the apples and serve coated in sauce.

aligot-aubrac.d: Mashed potato beaten vigorously with fresh tome cheese from the Aubrac until it forms a stretchy, elastic ribbon that pulls for metres, a speciality of the burons, the high-pasture herders' huts.
s: Boil the whole potatoes in salted water until tender, peel while still hot.
Mash into a very smooth, lump-free purée with a ricer.
Return the purée to the pan over low heat, stir in butter, cream and crushed garlic.
Gradually add the fresh tome cheese cut into strips, beating vigorously with a wooden spatula.
Keep beating continuously until the aligot forms a long, stretchy elastic ribbon, serve immediately.

culurgiones.d: Hand-sealed ravioli pinched into a braided wheat-ear pattern, filled with mashed potato, pecorino and wild mint, whose precise folding distinguishes each village of Sardinia's Ogliastra region.
s: Knead flour, water and a pinch of salt into a firm, smooth dough, rest 30 minutes under a cloth.
Mash the cooked potato with grated pecorino, chopped mint, garlic and olive oil into a smooth filling.
Roll the dough thin, cut circles, place a spoonful of filling in the centre of each.
Close each disc by pinching the edges in small successive folds to form the characteristic braided pattern.
Poach the culurgiones in salted boiling water a few minutes until they float, serve coated in tomato sauce.

nduja-pasta.d: A fermented pork and Calabrian chilli sausage, so soft it spreads like a paste, melted into a tomato sauce until it dyes the pasta a burning red, a speciality of Spilinga now exported worldwide.
s: Heat the olive oil with crushed garlic until fragrant.
Add the crumbled 'nduja, let it melt over low heat until it dyes the oil red.
Pour in the tomato sauce, simmer 15 minutes over low heat.
Cook the pasta al dente in well-salted water, drain reserving a little cooking water.
Toss the pasta with the sauce, adding a little cooking water if needed, scatter with pecorino and parsley.

canederli.d: Large dumplings of stale bread, smoked bacon and cheese bound with egg, poached then served floating in a clear beef broth or simply buttered, an alpine speciality betraying the Austrian influence on Trentino-Alto Adige.
s: Cut the stale bread into small dice, soak in warm milk 15 minutes.
Fry the diced bacon until crisp, add it to the soaked bread.
Stir in beaten eggs, flour and chopped parsley, mix into a homogeneous but not overly compact mass.
Shape large dumplings with wet hands, let rest 15 minutes so they hold together.
Poach the canederli in simmering beef broth 15 minutes, serve floating in the broth or drained with melted butter.

goya-champuru.d: A stir-fry of bitter melon, firm tofu and pork belly, bound with beaten egg, whose name champurū means "mixture" in the Okinawan dialect — an everyday dish of the island famed for its residents' exceptional longevity.
s: Cut the bitter melon in half, deseed and slice thinly, salt to draw out bitterness 10 minutes then rinse.
Press the firm tofu, cut into cubes, dry-fry until golden and set aside.
Fry the thinly sliced pork belly until crisp.
Add the drained bitter melon, stir-fry 3 minutes, return the golden tofu, season with soy sauce.
Pour the beaten egg over the top, let it set without stirring too much, scatter with bonito flakes and serve.

takoyaki.d: Small dashi-based batter balls, cooked in a plate with hemispherical moulds with a piece of octopus hidden inside, flipped with a precise pick motion, topped with sweet-savoury sauce and mayonnaise.
s: Mix flour, dashi and beaten eggs into a smooth, liquid batter, rest 20 minutes.
Cut the octopus into small cubes, chop the scallion and pickled ginger.
Generously oil the heated takoyaki plate, pour the batter into each hemispherical mould until slightly overflowing.
Drop a piece of octopus, scallion and ginger into each well before the batter fully sets.
Flip each ball halfway through with a fine pick to form a perfect sphere, top with sauce, mayonnaise and bonito flakes.

jingisukan.d: Lamb and mutton grilled on a domed plate shaped like a Mongolian helmet, surrounded by vegetables cooking in the fat that drips to the edges, a convivial Hokkaido dish named after Genghis Khan.
s: Prepare the marinade by blending soy sauce, mirin, garlic and grated apple.
Marinate thinly sliced lamb in half the sauce for 30 minutes.
Heat the domed plate, arrange the cut vegetables around the lower rim where fat will flow.
Grill the marinated lamb on the domed centre of the plate a few minutes per side.
Mix the grilled lamb with the vegetables cooked in the drippings, serve with the remaining sauce for dipping.

cataplana-de-marisco.d: A stew of clams, shrimp and chouriço simmered in a shell-shaped copper vessel that clamps shut, the steam cooking everything sealed inside, a culinary symbol of the Algarve born from exchanges with North Africa.
s: Soak the clams in salted water 1 hour to purge their sand.
Fry sliced onion, garlic and pepper in the base of the open cataplana.
Add crushed tomato and sliced chouriço, simmer 10 minutes.
Place clams and shrimp on top, splash with white wine, seal the cataplana shut.
Cook 12 minutes over high heat without opening, open at the table and scatter with coriander.

espetada-madeirense.d: Large cubes of beef marinated in garlic and bay, threaded onto a fresh bay branch whittled to a point, hung above the table on a wrought-iron stand to be pulled straight onto the plate.
s: Cut the beef into large even cubes of about 4 cm.
Marinate with crushed garlic, crumbled bay leaf, salt and white wine for 4 hours.
Thread the cubes onto fresh bay branches whittled to a point.
Grill over hot embers, turning regularly, 10 to 12 minutes depending on desired doneness.
Hang the skewers above the table on a stand, serve with corn bread.

bolo-do-caco.d: A round flatbread made with sweet potato, cooked not in an oven but directly on a hot volcanic stone called a caco, split still steaming and spread with garlic butter on the streets of Madeira.
s: Cook and mash the sweet potato into a fine purée, let cool.
Knead flour, sweet potato purée, yeast, salt and warm water into a supple dough, let rise 1 hour.
Divide into balls, flatten each into a thick disc about 2 cm.
Cook on a hot stone or dry cast-iron pan, 5 minutes per side.
Mix melted butter, crushed garlic and parsley, spread generously on the still-hot bread split in two.

cozido-das-furnas.d: A pot of meats and vegetables sealed in a large cloth-wrapped cauldron, buried in the steaming volcanic ground of the Furnas crater and cooked for six hours by the island's geothermal heat alone.
s: Arrange all the meats and cured pork at the bottom of a large sturdy cloth cauldron.
Add cabbage cut into wedges, carrot, potato and sweet potato on top.
Seal the cauldron shut and bury it in a hole dug into the hot fumarole ground.
Let cook this way for 6 hours by the natural geothermal steam alone.
Dig up the cauldron, open it at the table and serve the tender meats and vegetables in their concentrated juices.

tripas-a-moda-do-porto.d: A stew of tripe, white beans and mixed meats, the dish that earned Porto's residents their nickname tripeiros after they legendarily gave away all their meat to the ships of Prince Henry the Navigator.
s: Soak the white beans overnight, cook separately until tender.
Clean the tripe thoroughly, blanch then cook 2 hours in water with carrot and onion.
Fry chorizo and pork belly, add the chicken pieces and brown.
Combine drained tripe, meats, cooked beans and cumin in one pot, simmer 45 minutes.
Serve with white rice, a hearty dish traditionally shared around a large table.

migas-alentejanas.d: Stale bread crumbled and pressed into a compact mass in pork fat, forming a golden crust with a soft interior, served in thick slices with grilled pork chops, a peasant dish of the Alentejo.
s: Crumble the stale bread very finely, sprinkle with warm salted water to slightly moisten.
Melt the pork fat in a large pan with crushed garlic and bay leaf.
Add the crumbled bread, press into a compact mass, cook over low heat, pressing regularly until a golden crust forms.
Separately grill the pork chops marinated in paprika.
Cut the migas into thick slices, serve with the grilled chops.

posta-mirandesa.d: A thick slice of Mirandesa veal, a local breed raised free-range on the border plateaus, simply grilled in olive oil and garlic to let the quality of the meat speak for itself.
s: Take the meat out of the fridge 1 hour before cooking so it reaches room temperature.
Heat a cast-iron plate over high heat with a little olive oil.
Sear the thick veal slices 3 minutes per side for a medium-rare doneness.
Drizzle with hot garlic and bay-infused olive oil at the end of cooking.
Serve with whole sautéed potatoes and coarse salt.

rojoes-a-moda-do-minho.d: Pork cubes marinated overnight in white wine, garlic and paprika, fried in their own fat until crisp outside and tender inside, served with pork tripe and chestnuts.
s: Cut the pork into cubes, marinate overnight with white wine, crushed garlic, paprika and bay leaf.
Drain the cubes reserving the marinade, brown them in their own fat over medium heat.
Add a little marinade during cooking to deglaze and flavour, let reduce.
Cook the chestnuts separately in water until tender.
Serve the browned pork with the chestnuts and fresh orange wedges to cut through the fat.

chanfana-da-beira.d: A young goat simmered for hours in thick, tannic red wine until the meat falls off the bone by itself, traditionally cooked in a black earthenware pot placed in a wood-fired bread oven.
s: Cut the young goat into large pieces, rub with crushed garlic and paprika.
Arrange in an earthenware pot with onion, bay leaf and pork fat.
Cover entirely with tannic red wine, close the pot.
Bake at a low 190°C for 4 hours in a wood-fired oven if possible.
Check the meat falls off the bone easily and the sauce has reduced, serve with corn bread.

bifana.d: A thin pork slice marinated in white wine, garlic and chilli, simmered in its juices until extremely tender, tucked into a small roll fresh from the oven, a popular sandwich devoured in two bites.
s: Cut the pork into thin slices, marinate at least 4 hours in white wine, garlic, bay leaf, paprika and chilli.
Cook the marinated slices over medium heat in a wide pan with their marinade.
Simmer uncovered until the sauce reduces and coats the meat, about 15 minutes.
Warm the small rolls in the oven a few minutes.
Fill each roll with pork slices coated in sauce and a dab of mustard.

ameijoas-a-bulhao-pato.d: Clams opened in minutes in a broth of garlic, fresh coriander and white wine, a recipe named after a 19th-century poet known for his gourmandise, eaten straight with the fingers and bread for mopping up.
s: Purge the clams in salted water at least 1 hour.
Heat the olive oil with sliced garlic and chilli until fragrant without colouring.
Add the drained clams and white wine, cover.
Cook over high heat 5 minutes, shaking the pan, until all the clams have opened.
Scatter generously with chopped fresh coriander, drizzle with a squeeze of lemon and serve with bread.

arroz-de-pato.d: Rice cooked in shredded duck broth, layered with chouriço and pork rind in an earthenware dish then baked until the top caramelises into a crackling crust, a quintessential Sunday dish.
s: Poach the whole duck with onion, carrot and bay leaf 1 hour until tender, shred the meat and reserve the broth.
Cook the rice in the strained duck broth to two-thirds done.
Layer half the rice in an earthenware dish, cover with shredded duck and sliced chouriço.
Cover with the rest of the rice, arrange the rind on top, moisten with a little broth.
Bake 20 minutes at 220°C until the top is golden and crackling, serve with orange zest.

feijoada-a-transmontana.d: A hearty stew of red beans and multiple smoked cured meats from Trás-os-Montes — chouriço, alheira, pig's ear and trotter — simmered for hours so the smoky flavours fully permeate the beans.
s: Soak the red beans overnight, drain.
Desalt the pig's ear and tail by blanching in boiling water.
Combine beans, salted meats, chorizo, onion, carrot and bay leaf in a large pot, cover with water.
Simmer covered 2 hours over low heat until the beans and meats are tender.
Adjust seasoning, let rest 10 minutes before serving piping hot.

polvo-a-lagareiro.d: A whole octopus boiled until tender then roasted, tentacles splayed like a star, drowned in a generous flood of virgin olive oil after cooking, surrounded by hand-crushed roasted potatoes.
s: Freeze then thaw the octopus to tenderise it, boil 40 minutes with bay leaf until tender.
Roast whole potatoes in their skins until tender.
Place the whole boiled octopus in an oven dish, surround with the potatoes lightly crushed by hand.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and scatter crushed garlic, bake 15 minutes at 220°C.
Scatter with fresh parsley and serve immediately, well oiled.

sopa-da-pedra.d: A hearty soup of red beans, cured meats and vegetables, born from a legend of a beggar convincing a village to cook a soup from a plain stone by adding, one ingredient at a time, everything needed for a real feast.
s: Soak the red beans overnight, cook halfway.
Add chorizo and desalted pig's ear, simmer 40 minutes until tender.
Add diced potato and shredded cabbage, cook another 20 minutes.
Adjust seasoning with crushed garlic, let reduce to a thick consistency.
Traditionally place a smooth clean stone at the bottom of the bowl as a nod to the legend, scatter with coriander and serve scalding.

queijo-serra-broa.d: A creamy sheep's milk cheese with a runny heart, curdled with thistle flower according to an age-old method, served by simply slicing off the top to dip a spoon in, paired with dense corn bread called broa.
s: Knead cornmeal, wheat flour, yeast, salt and warm water into a dense, sticky dough.
Let the dough rise 1 hour under a cloth in a warm spot.
Shape into a large round loaf, bake 40 minutes at 200°C until the crust is thick and dark.
Let the sheep's cheese rest at room temperature 30 minutes so its texture softens.
Cut off the top of the cheese like a lid, serve with thick slices of still-warm broa.

toucinho-do-ceu.d: A dense convent cake of ground almonds and egg yolks, whose name means "bacon from heaven" despite containing no trace of it, a legacy of nuns who used the whites to starch their headdresses.
s: Make a thick syrup with sugar and water, boil 8 minutes until it threads.
Finely blend the almonds, stir into the hot syrup off the heat, let cool slightly.
Beat the egg yolks, gradually whisk into the warm almond paste.
Add lemon zest, pour into a buttered mould.
Bake in a water bath 35 minutes at 170°C until barely set in the centre, let cool before unmoulding.

favas-a-portuguesa.d: Fresh spring broad beans simmered with chouriço, coriander and a poached egg dropped in at the last moment, a rustic Ribatejo dish celebrating the arrival of early spring produce after winter.
s: Shell the fresh broad beans, sweat sliced onion and garlic in olive oil.
Add the sliced chorizo, fry 3 minutes.
Add the beans, moisten with a little water, simmer covered 20 minutes until tender.
Poach the eggs separately in simmering vinegared water.
Serve the beans scattered with fresh coriander, a poached egg placed on each portion.

confit-de-canard.d: Duck legs salted then slowly cooked submerged in their own fat until extremely tender, an ancestral preservation technique from the Périgord that became a classic with golden, crackling skin.
s: Rub the duck legs generously with coarse salt, crushed garlic and thyme, let rest 24 hours chilled.
Rinse and thoroughly dry the legs to remove excess salt.
Fully submerge them in melted duck fat with the bay leaf.
Cook at a very low temperature for 3 hours, the fat should never simmer hard.
Crisp the skin in a pan before serving with potatoes sautéed in duck fat.

baeckeoffe.d: Three meats marinated in Riesling with potato and onion, layered in a terrine sealed with a rope of dough, which Alsatian farmwives carried to the baker's oven on Mondays, the day of washing.
s: Cut the three meats into large chunks, marinate overnight in Riesling with onion, bay leaf and juniper.
Peel and thinly slice the potatoes.
Layer in a terrine: potatoes, marinated meat, potatoes, ending with potatoes.
Pour the marinade over the top, seal the lid with a rope of flour-and-water dough.
Bake 3 hours at 160°C without opening, break the dough seal at the table to release the aromas.

biscuits-roses-de-reims.d: A dry biscuit tinted a delicate pink, born in the 17th century from Champagne bakers seeking to use their ovens' residual heat, today traditionally dipped into a glass of champagne.
s: Separate the whites from the yolks, whisk the whites to stiff peaks with half the sugar.
Beat the yolks with the remaining sugar and vanilla until pale, add a few drops of pink colouring.
Gently fold in the flour then the whisked whites, without deflating the batter.
Pipe finger shapes onto a tray, dust generously with icing sugar.
Bake 12 minutes at 180°C, let dry outside the oven before serving with a glass of champagne.

tarte-tatin.d: A caramelised apple tart baked upside down then flipped at the last moment, born from a famous mishap by the Tatin sisters who forgot the pastry and hastily added it over the already-cooking fruit.
s: Knead a shortcrust pastry with flour, butter, egg and a little water, let rest 30 minutes chilled.
Melt the sugar dry in an oven-safe pan until a golden caramel.
Add the butter to the caramel, arrange the peeled apples cut into tight wedges on top.
Cook the apples in the caramel over low heat 15 minutes, cover with the rolled pastry, tucking in the edges.
Bake 30 minutes at 200°C, let cool 10 minutes then flip onto a plate, serve with fresh cream.

poulet-au-vin-jaune.n: Chicken with vin jaune and morels
poulet-au-vin-jaune.d: A farmhouse chicken simmered in Jura's vin jaune, an oxidative wine with walnut notes aged six years under a yeast veil, paired with rehydrated dried morels and a velvety cream — the most prestigious pairing of the Jura.
s: Soak the dried morels in a little warm water 30 minutes, strain and reserve the liquid.
Brown the chicken pieces in butter, set aside.
Sweat the sliced shallot, deglaze with vin jaune, let reduce by half.
Return the chicken, add the morels and their strained liquid, simmer covered 35 minutes.
Stir in the cream at the end of cooking, let thicken slightly and serve piping hot.

salade-lyonnaise.d: A bitter frisée salad topped with crispy lardons and a poached egg whose runny yolk mingles with a warm vinegar dressing, a hearty Lyonnaise bouchon dish despite its light appearance.
s: Wash and thoroughly dry the frisée, place it in a large salad bowl.
Fry the lardons dry until crisp, reserve the rendered fat.
Rub toasted bread croutons with garlic.
Deglaze the hot bacon fat with vinegar and mustard for the warm dressing, pour over the frisée.
Poach the eggs, place one on each plate with lardons and croutons, serve immediately.

soupe-au-pistou.d: A soup of summer vegetables and white and red beans, crowned just before serving with a spoonful of pistou — basil, garlic and parmesan pounded with olive oil — Provençal cousin of Genoese pesto.
s: Cook the white and red beans separately until tender.
Bring a large volume of water to the boil, add diced potato and zucchini, cook 15 minutes.
Add crushed tomato, cut green beans, cooked beans and pasta, cook another 15 minutes.
Pound basil, garlic and parmesan in a mortar, gradually work in the olive oil until a smooth paste forms.
Serve the soup scalding, a spoonful of pistou placed in the centre of each bowl just before eating.

potjevleesch.d: A cold terrine of four meats — rabbit, chicken, pork and veal — simmered separately then set together in a white vinegar jelly, a Flemish speciality served sliced with hot fries.
s: Cut the four meats into large chunks, arrange in a large pot with onion and bay leaf.
Cover with water and white vinegar, simmer covered 2h30 over low heat until the meats are very tender.
Drain the meats reserving the broth, arrange in a terrine.
Reduce the broth, dissolve the gelatine in it, pour over the meats in the terrine.
Let set in the fridge at least 12 hours, unmould and serve sliced cold with fries.

brandade-de-morue.d: Desalted flaked salt cod whipped with olive oil like a mayonnaise, until forming a white, velvety mousse, a legacy of exchanges between northern fishermen and Mediterranean olive-oil producers.
s: Desalt the cod 24 hours, changing the water several times.
Poach the cod in simmering water 10 minutes, drain and flake, removing skin and bones.
Mash the flaked cod with garlic, whip in olive oil gradually as you would a mayonnaise.
Add warm milk gradually to soften the texture, season with nutmeg.
Serve warm with toasted bread croutons, as a starter or light dish.

kig-ha-farz.d: A Breton pot-au-feu where salted beef and vegetables simmer, alongside a buckwheat far pudding cooked wrapped in a cloth bag which, once unmoulded and crumbled, is drizzled with browned butter and gwell, local fermented milk.
s: Cook the salted beef and bacon in a large volume of water 2 hours until tender.
Add cabbage in wedges and carrot, simmer another 40 minutes.
Prepare the far by mixing buckwheat flour, eggs, milk and raisins into a liquid batter.
Pour the batter into a clean cloth bag loosely tied, plunge it into the broth to cook 1 hour.
Unmould the far, crumble it with a fork, drizzle with melted butter and serve with the meat and vegetables.

axoa-espelette.d: Veal coarsely chopped by knife, simmered with green peppers and the famous Espelette pepper that hangs in garlands along the village façades throughout autumn, a deeply coloured and fragrant Basque dish.
s: Chop the veal coarsely by knife into small irregular pieces.
Sweat the onion and sliced green peppers until tender.
Add the veal, brown it over high heat a few minutes.
Add crushed tomato, garlic, Espelette pepper and white wine, simmer covered 30 minutes.
Adjust the chilli seasoning to taste, serve with fried Espelette peppers on the side.

fiadone.d: A soft cake made with brocciu, a fresh Corsican sheep's or goat's milk cheese, scented with lemon zest, with a texture between flan and cheesecake, served warm or cold at the end of an island meal.
s: Mash the brocciu with a fork until smooth.
Beat the whole eggs with the sugar until pale and doubled in volume.
Fold the mashed brocciu, lemon zest and brandy into the mixture.
Pour into a buttered mould, bake 35 minutes at 180°C until golden and barely set in the centre.
Let cool before unmoulding, serve warm or chilled depending on the season.

potee-auvergnate.d: A country pot-au-feu combining salt pork, sausage and green cabbage with root vegetables from the Massif Central, simmered for hours in a large cast-iron pot once hung on the hearth's chain.
s: Desalt the salt pork several hours, changing the water.
Cook it in a large volume of water 1 hour with bay leaf.
Add carrot, turnip and leek, simmer another 45 minutes.
Add cabbage in wedges, potato and sausage, cook 30 more minutes until everything is tender.
Serve the meat and vegetables drained in large soup plates, with a little broth and mustard on the side.

diots-au-vin-blanc.d: Small Savoyard pork sausages simmered in Apremont white wine with onion and bay leaf, until the skin soaks up the wine, traditionally served with creamy polenta or potatoes.
s: Lightly prick the sausages with a fork to prevent them bursting.
Brown them in a pot with the sliced onion.
Moisten with white wine, add the bay leaf, simmer covered 30 minutes over low heat.
Meanwhile, prepare a creamy polenta by stirring cornmeal into boiling salted water, stir in butter and grated Comté.
Serve the diots coated in their cooking juices over a bed of melting polenta.

entrecote-bordelaise.d: An entrecôte traditionally grilled over vine cuttings for a subtle smoky aroma, coated in a sauce reduced with Bordeaux red wine, shallot and beef marrow, rich and full-bodied.
s: Grill the entrecôte over hot embers, ideally vine cuttings, to the desired doneness.
Let the meat rest under foil a few minutes.
Sweat the finely chopped shallot in a little butter.
Deglaze with red wine, reduce by two thirds, add the beef broth and diced marrow, let melt.
Finish the sauce off the heat with cold butter, coat the sliced entrecôte and serve immediately.

tripes-mode-de-caen.d: Beef tripe simmered for eight hours in cider and calvados with veal foot for gelatine, in an earthenware pot sealed with dough, a Norman recipe once praised all the way to Louis XIV's table.
s: Clean the tripe thoroughly, cut into even squares.
Arrange tripe and cut veal foot in a large earthenware pot with carrot, onion, leek and bay leaf.
Moisten with cider and calvados, seal hermetically with a rope of flour-and-water dough.
Bake at a very low 90°C for 8 hours without opening.
Break the dough seal at the table, skim the surface slightly and serve scalding in soup plates.

pot-au-feu.d: A clear beef broth simmered for hours with marrow bone, carrot, leek and turnip, served in two successive courses — first the broth with vermicelli, then the meat and vegetables — a pillar of the French table for centuries.
s: Plunge the beef and marrow bone into a large pot of cold water, slowly bring to the boil, skimming.
Stud the onion with cloves, add with carrot, leek and turnip, simmer covered 3 hours.
Check the meat's tenderness with a fork, it should pull apart easily.
Strain part of the broth, cook the vermicelli in it for the first course.
Serve the meat and vegetables as a second course with coarse salt, pickles and mustard.

rougail-saucisse.d: Smoked sausages simmered in a tomato sauce with ginger, garlic and chilli, the most-eaten everyday dish of Réunion, served with white rice and grains — lentils or red beans.
s: Blanch the smoked sausages 5 minutes in boiling water to remove excess fat, drain.
Fry the sliced onion, garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add crushed tomato, thyme and chilli, simmer 10 minutes into a thick sauce.
Add the blanched sausages cut into chunks, simmer covered 25 minutes.
Cook rice and lentils separately, serve the rougail with both on the side.

colombo-de-poulet.d: A chicken curry with colombo spice blend, an Indian mix brought by 19th-century Tamil indentured workers, simmered with potato, eggplant and a splash of lime juice, a Creole dish that became emblematic of Martinique.
s: Rub the chicken pieces with colombo spice, marinate 1 hour.
Fry the sliced onion and garlic, add the marinated chicken, brown.
Add potato and eggplant in chunks, moisten with water and coconut milk.
Add the whole scotch bonnet without piercing it to flavour without too much heat, simmer 30 minutes.
Remove the chilli, drizzle with a splash of lime juice and serve with white rice.

accras-de-morue.d: Small fritters of desalted, flaked salt cod in a batter spiked with chilli and scallion, fried until an irregular golden crust forms, an unmissable appetiser at every Caribbean family gathering.
s: Desalt the cod 24 hours, changing the water, flake finely without cooking.
Prepare a fritter batter with flour, yeast, egg and warm water, let rise 30 minutes.
Fold in the flaked cod, chopped scallion, chilli and garlic.
Shape small balls with a spoon, slide directly into hot oil at 180°C.
Fry until golden and puffed, drain on paper towel and serve hot as an appetiser.

beef-stroganoff.d: Thin strips of beef quickly seared and coated in a sauce of smetana cream and mustard, a dish created in the 19th century for Count Stroganov's table, simple enough to prepare that it became a worldwide classic.
s: Cut the beef into thin, even strips.
Fry sliced onion and mushrooms in butter until golden, set aside.
Sear the beef strips over very high heat just a few seconds per side.
Return the onion and mushrooms, add smetana cream, mustard and a little broth, mix off the strong heat.
Warm through without boiling to avoid curdling the cream, serve immediately with sautéed potatoes.

olivier-salad.d: A salad of potato, carrot, peas, pickles and diced meat bound with mayonnaise, created by a Belgian chef in Moscow whose exact recipe remained secret, now the essential dish of Russian New Year.
s: Cook potato, carrot and eggs separately in water until tender, let cool.
Cut potato, carrot, hard-boiled eggs, pickles and meat into small, even dice.
Combine all the dice in a large bowl with the peas.
Add the mayonnaise and a dab of mustard, mix gently to coat well without crushing.
Chill at least 2 hours before serving, ideally overnight so the flavours meld.

pelmeni-sibirskie.d: Small dumplings of mixed beef and pork, hand-pinched then frozen in large batches outdoors in the Siberian cold, a winter reserve poached as needed through the long frozen months.
s: Knead flour, egg, water and salt into a firm dough, rest 30 minutes under a cloth.
Mix minced beef and pork with grated onion, salt and pepper into a smooth filling.
Roll the dough thin, cut circles, fill and fold, pinching the edges firmly into a small ear shape.
Freeze the uncooked pelmeni on a floured tray if preparing a reserve.
Poach in salted boiling water 8 minutes until they float, serve with smetana cream and dill.

syrniki.d: Small golden patties of tvorog, Russia's granular fresh cheese similar to cottage cheese, mixed with egg and a little flour, served warm with smetana cream and berry jam for breakfast.
s: Mash the tvorog with a fork to remove large lumps.
Stir in egg, sugar, vanilla and most of the flour into a supple but firm batter.
Shape small round patties, lightly dust in the remaining flour.
Brown them in butter over medium heat, 3 minutes per side until a golden crust forms.
Serve warm with smetana cream and berry jam on the side.

blini-ikra.d: Small thick yeast-leavened buckwheat pancakes, soft and slightly tangy, topped with smetana cream and salmon or sturgeon roe, a festive dish that traditionally accompanied Maslenitsa celebrations.
s: Dissolve the yeast in a little warm milk, let foam 10 minutes.
Mix buckwheat and wheat flours, stir in the yeast mixture, remaining warm milk and beaten eggs into a smooth batter.
Let the batter rise 45 minutes in a warm spot until doubled.
Cook small thick pancakes in a buttered pan, 2 minutes per side until golden.
Serve warm topped with smetana cream and a spoonful of salmon roe on each blini.

okroshka.d: A cold summer soup of raw vegetables, hard-boiled egg and diced meat, drowned in slightly sparkling fermented kvass or kefir, served icy to cool down during the rare hot days of the short Russian summer.
s: Cut cucumber, hard-boiled eggs, meat and radish into small, very even dice.
Finely chop the scallion and dill.
Combine all the cut ingredients in a large bowl, mix.
Pour the cold kvass over the top until generously covered, add a spoonful of diluted mustard.
Add a spoonful of smetana cream to each individual bowl, serve immediately, well chilled.

shchi.d: A soup of fresh or fermented cabbage simmered with pork and root vegetables, the oldest everyday dish of the Russian table, of which an old saying claims that it and kasha, porridge, are our food.
s: Cook the pork pieces in a large volume of water 1 hour until tender, skim regularly.
Add sliced onion and carrot, simmer 15 minutes.
Add fermented cabbage and diced potato, cook another 25 minutes.
Season with bay leaf, adjust salt according to the cabbage's acidity.
Serve scalding with a spoonful of smetana cream and fresh chopped dill on each bowl.

ukha.d: A clear, limpid fish soup, never thickened or clouded, traditionally made with several different fish including Volga delta sturgeon, finished with a touch of vodka just before serving.
s: Poach the whole fish in water with whole onion and bay leaf 20 minutes, skim carefully to keep the broth clear.
Remove the fish, flake the flesh removing skin and bones, strain the broth.
Reheat the strained broth, add potato and carrot in chunks, cook 15 minutes.
Return the flaked fish to the broth, warm through without boiling.
Add a splash of vodka just before serving, scatter with fresh dill.

kulebyaka.d: A long, golden pastry pie enclosing several distinct layers of fish, rice, hard-boiled egg and mushrooms, each separated by a thin pancake to keep moisture from soaking the puff pastry.
s: Cook the rice until tender, hard-boil the eggs, fry sliced mushrooms and onion.
Prepare thin pancakes with flour, egg, milk and a little melted butter.
Roll out the puff pastry into a large rectangle, place a pancake then a layer of rice in the centre.
Layer salmon, pancake, mushrooms, sliced hard-boiled egg and dill, separating each layer with a pancake.
Close the pastry into a long golden pie, bake 35 minutes at 200°C until well browned, let rest before slicing.

solyanka.d: A spicy, tangy soup mixing several types of smoked meats and cured sausage, olives, capers and pickled cucumbers, with contrasting flavours intentionally meant as a reviving remedy after an overly wet evening.
s: Fry sliced onion in a little bacon fat.
Add the various meats cut into strips and the tomato paste, fry 5 minutes.
Moisten with water or broth, add sliced pickles, olives and capers, simmer 25 minutes.
Adjust the tang with a little pickle brine if needed.
Serve scalding with a lemon slice and a spoonful of smetana cream on each bowl.

chak-chak.d: Small pieces of fried dough browned then bound together in warm honey, shaped into a decorative pyramid, a Tatar festive cake invariably presented at weddings and births.
s: Knead flour, eggs, sugar and a pinch of salt into a firm dough, let rest 20 minutes.
Roll the dough thin, cut into thin strips then small irregular pea-sized pieces.
Fry the pieces in small batches in hot oil at 180°C until golden and puffed.
Warm the honey until fluid without letting it caramelise.
Mix the drained fried pieces into the warm honey, immediately shape into a pyramid on a platter, let harden before serving.

azu-po-tatarski.d: Strips of beef simmered with pickled cucumbers and potato in a spiced tomato sauce, a Tatar speciality where the tang of the pickles cuts through the richness of the long-cooked meat.
s: Cut the beef into thick strips, brown vigorously in a pot.
Add sliced onion, fry until translucent.
Add tomato paste and broth, simmer covered 40 minutes until tender.
Add potato in wedges and pickles in strips, cook another 20 minutes.
Add the crushed garlic right at the end of cooking, adjust seasoning and serve scalding.

pirozhki.d: Small yeasted dough turnovers filled with meat, cabbage or potato, fried or baked, once hawked at train stations and platforms, the quintessential travel snack across all of Russia.
s: Knead flour, yeast, warm milk, egg and salt into a supple dough, let rise 1 hour.
Fry minced beef or shredded cabbage with onion for the filling of your choice, let cool slightly.
Divide the dough into balls, flatten each into a disc, fill with filling.
Close into a turnover, pinching the edges well to seal.
Fry in hot oil until golden or bake 20 minutes at 190°C, serve hot.

kholodets.d: A cold pork meat jelly simmered so long that the collagen from trotters and shanks naturally turns into aspic, with no added gelatine, served sliced with horseradish or sharp mustard.
s: Soak the pig's trotters and shanks a few hours, brush thoroughly.
Cook in a large volume of water at a very gentle simmer 6 hours with onion, carrot and bay leaf, never boiling hard.
Skim regularly, salt at the end of cooking.
Shred the cooked meat, arrange with crushed garlic at the bottom of moulds or a dish.
Strain the collagen-rich broth, pour over the meat, let set in the fridge at least 8 hours, unmould and serve with horseradish.

shashlyk-kubanskiy.d: Pork cubes marinated overnight in onion, vinegar and spices, grilled on wide flat skewers over fruitwood embers, a festive tradition of Russia's fertile south near the Caucasus.
s: Cut the pork into large even cubes.
Mix with onion sliced into thick rounds, vinegar, bay leaf, pepper and crushed coriander.
Let marinate overnight chilled, stirring occasionally.
Thread the cubes onto wide flat skewers, alternating with rounds of marinated onion.
Grill over hot embers 12 to 15 minutes, turning regularly, serve with the grilled onions.

pozy-buryatskie.d: Large Mongol-Buryat steamed dumplings closed into a pleated crown with exactly twenty-five folds, filled with fatty meat and onion, from which the scalding juice is first sipped through a small hole before biting in.
s: Knead flour, water and salt into a firm dough, let rest 30 minutes.
Mix coarsely minced beef and pork with very finely chopped onion and a little water to make the filling juicy.
Roll out the dough, cut fairly large circles, fill generously with filling.
Close into a pleated crown, pinching the edges all around, leaving a small hole at the top.
Steam 18 minutes, let cool 2 minutes, sip the juice through the hole before eating the rest.

stroganina.d: A freshwater fish frozen solid by Yakutia's extreme cold, shaved into paper-thin curls with a knife right at the table, dipped in a mix of salt and pepper, eaten at once before it thaws.
s: Use a freshwater fish frozen entirely solid, never previously thawed.
Hold the frozen fish firmly wrapped in a cloth for grip.
Shave very thin curls using a well-sharpened knife, directly over a cold plate.
Mix fine salt and freshly ground black pepper in a small dish.
Dip each curl of frozen fish into the salt and pepper just before eating, while still hard and cold.

medovik.d: A layer cake of thin honey-dough sheets stacked with velvety smetana cream, left to rest overnight so the layers soften as they absorb the cream, born from a pastry chef trying to please a tsarina who hated honey.
s: Melt honey, butter and sugar in a bain-marie, add the baking soda off the heat until it foams.
Stir in the beaten eggs then gradually the flour into a supple, still-warm dough.
Divide into 8 balls, roll each very thin, bake each disc 4 minutes at 200°C until golden.
Whip the smetana cream with icing sugar until velvety.
Stack the pastry discs, spreading cream between each, chill overnight before serving sliced.

pashka.d: A cold dessert of tvorog, butter and candied fruit pressed into a pyramidal wooden mould marked with the letters XB, an Orthodox Easter symbol blessed at church before being served in thin wedges on Easter morning.
s: Pass the tvorog through a fine sieve for a perfectly smooth texture.
Beat the softened butter with sugar until creamy, add the egg yolks one at a time.
Mix with the sieved tvorog, smetana cream and vanilla.
Fold in candied fruit and crushed almonds.
Line a pyramidal mould with clean cloth, fill and press firmly, refrigerate under weight 24 hours before unmoulding.

rassolnik.d: A tangy soup with pickled cucumbers and pearl barley, whose pickle-brine acidity added at the end of cooking cuts through the tenderness of the pork or beef kidneys traditionally used.
s: Soak the kidneys in milk 1 hour to remove their strong smell, rinse and dice.
Cook the pearl barley separately until tender.
Fry the kidneys, onion and carrot, moisten with water, simmer 25 minutes.
Add potato, diced pickles and cooked barley, cook another 15 minutes.
Add pickle brine at the end of cooking to taste, scatter with dill and serve scalding.

vareniki-vishnya.d: Large sweet dumplings filled with pitted cherries macerated in sugar, poached then served warm drowned in smetana cream, a summer dessert that tints the dough a light pink during cooking.
s: Knead flour, egg, water and a pinch of salt into a supple dough, let rest 30 minutes.
Pit the cherries, mix with sugar, let macerate 20 minutes to release their juice.
Roll the dough thin, cut fairly wide circles.
Fill each circle with a few drained cherries, close by firmly pinching the edges into a half-moon.
Poach in boiling water 6 minutes until they float, drain and serve with melted butter and smetana cream.

gurievskaya-kasha.d: A sweet semolina porridge built up in successive layers with the creamy skin that forms on the surface of oven-warmed milk, scattered with dried fruit and nuts, an imperial 19th-century dessert named after a gourmet finance minister.
s: Pour the milk into a wide oven dish, bake at low temperature until a creamy skin forms on the surface, gently lift it off and repeat several times.
Cook the semolina in the remaining sweetened milk until thickened, flavour with vanilla.
Arrange a layer of semolina in a dish, cover with reserved milk skins and crushed dried fruit.
Repeat the layers alternating semolina, milk skins and dried fruit until used up.
Drizzle with warm honey, pass briefly under the grill to lightly caramelise the top, serve warm.

lobster-roll.d: Freshly shelled lobster meat, barely bound with mayonnaise or simply melted butter depending on the school of thought, piled into a hot-dog bun toasted on the sides, an emblematic summer sandwich of Maine.
s: Cook the lobster in salted boiling water 10 minutes, let cool then shell.
Cut the meat into large even chunks.
Gently mix with mayonnaise, finely chopped celery and a squeeze of lemon.
Toast the buttered buns on both cut sides until golden.
Generously fill each bun with lobster meat, scatter with chives and serve immediately.

buffalo-wings.d: Chicken wings fried plain then drowned in a scorching butter and hot sauce, born in 1964 at a Buffalo bar to use up an unexpected delivery, served with celery sticks and blue cheese dip to temper the heat.
s: Thoroughly dry the chicken wings, fry in hot oil 12 minutes until well browned and crisp.
Melt the butter, mix it into the hot sauce while still warm to emulsify.
Drain the fried wings, plunge them into the scorching sauce, tossing to coat well.
Prepare the blue cheese dip by mixing crumbled blue cheese, sour cream and a little vinegar.
Serve the wings immediately with celery sticks and the blue cheese dip on the side.

deep-dish-pizza.d: A thick pizza baked in a high-sided pan like a pie, layered upside down with cheese under the tomato sauce to keep it from burning during the 35 minutes of baking needed, a speciality born in Chicago in the 1940s.
s: Knead flour, cornmeal, yeast, olive oil and warm water into a supple dough, let rise 1 hour.
Roll the thick dough into a well-oiled high-sided pan, bringing it up the sides.
Arrange sliced mozzarella directly on the dough.
Add cooked crumbled sausage, then the thick tomato sauce seasoned with oregano on top.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes at 220°C until golden crust, scatter with parmesan and let rest 10 minutes before cutting.

chicago-hot-dog.d: A poached all-beef sausage nestled in a poppy-seed bun, topped with a precise and untouchable list of seven condiments — mustard, onion, bright green relish, tomato, pickle, sport pepper and celery salt — never ketchup.
s: Poach the beef sausages in simmering water 6 minutes without boiling.
Steam the poppy-seed buns to soften slightly.
Place each sausage in a bun, drizzle mustard in a zigzag.
Top in order with finely chopped onion, green relish, tomato wedges, a whole pickle spear.
Finish with a pinch of celery salt and a sport pepper, serve immediately, never adding ketchup.

crab-cakes-maryland.d: Patties of Chesapeake Bay blue crab meat, barely bound with breadcrumbs and mayonnaise to let the crab dominate, pan-fried until golden, seasoned with the Old Bay spice blend emblematic of Maryland.
s: Carefully check the crab meat to remove any shell fragments.
Gently mix with breadcrumbs, mayonnaise, egg, mustard and Old Bay seasoning, without overworking to keep large lumps.
Shape thick patties by hand, chill 30 minutes so they hold together.
Brown the patties in butter over medium heat, 4 minutes per side.
Scatter with fresh parsley and serve with a lemon wedge and tartar sauce.

shrimp-and-grits.d: A creamy cheese-and-butter corn porridge, topped with shrimp sautéed with bacon and Cajun spices, a Lowcountry fishermen's dish elevated in a few decades to national gastronomic speciality.
s: Bring the milk to a boil, whisk in the grits in a stream to avoid lumps.
Cook over low heat 20 minutes, stirring regularly, until creamy, stir in cheddar cheese and butter.
Fry the diced bacon until crisp, set aside.
Sauté the shrimp seasoned with Cajun spice and garlic in the bacon fat until pink, 4 minutes.
Serve the shrimp and bacon over the creamy grits, scatter with chopped scallion.

kentucky-hot-brown.d: An open turkey sandwich drowned in cheesy mornay sauce, broiled with crispy bacon slices and tomato, invented in the 1920s by a Louisville hotel chef to feed hungry dancers after midnight.
s: Make a roux with butter and flour, moisten with hot milk, whisking until a smooth thick sauce forms.
Stir in the grated gruyère off the heat until melted, season.
Place a slice of bread in an individual dish, cover with thick turkey slices.
Coat generously with mornay sauce, add tomato slices and grated parmesan on top.
Broil a few minutes until golden and bubbling, garnish with crispy bacon and serve immediately, piping hot.

chicken-and-waffles.d: Extra-crispy fried chicken set directly on a soft waffle, drizzled with maple syrup for a sweet-savoury contrast, a dish born in Harlem's jazz clubs where people ate between late dinner and breakfast.
s: Marinate the chicken in buttermilk at least 4 hours.
Drain, dredge in flour seasoned with cayenne, fry at 175°C 15 minutes until golden and crisp.
Prepare the waffle batter by mixing flour, eggs, milk and melted butter.
Cook the waffles in a hot waffle iron until golden and crisp.
Place the fried chicken on the warm waffles, drizzle generously with maple syrup and serve immediately.

new-york-cheesecake.d: A dense, smooth cheesecake made with cream cheese, baked in a water bath on a thin crumbled biscuit crust, whose tall, compact texture radically contrasts with lighter European versions.
s: Blitz the biscuits into fine crumbs, mix with melted butter and press into the base of a springform pan.
Beat the cream cheese until smooth, gradually add the sugar.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating minimally to avoid incorporating too much air, then the cream, vanilla and lemon zest.
Pour over the crust, bake in a water bath 55 minutes at 160°C until barely wobbly in the centre.
Let cool in the turned-off oven with the door ajar, then chill at least 6 hours before unmoulding.

pastrami-on-rye.d: Beef brisket cured in a spiced brine then long-smoked and steamed, sliced thick and piled high between two slices of rye bread, a legacy of Eastern European Jewish delicatessens.
s: Rub the brisket with coarse salt, crushed garlic and spices, cure chilled 5 days, turning daily.
Rinse thoroughly, coat with a thick crust of cracked pepper and coriander.
Cold-smoke several hours then hot-smoke until a black crust forms.
Steam 3 hours until extremely tender.
Slice very thin against the grain, pile generously between two slices of rye bread with mustard, serve with pickles.

cuban-sandwich-miami.d: Roast pork, ham, Swiss cheese, pickle and mustard pressed in Cuban bread until the cheese melts and the crust turns crisp, a sandwich forged by the Cuban communities of Ybor City and Miami.
s: Roast or reheat the shredded or sliced pork.
Split the Cuban bread in two, spread mustard on both sides.
Fill with pork, ham, sliced Swiss cheese and pickle strips.
Butter the outside of the sandwich, press in a hot plancha or panini press.
Cook 5 minutes while pressing until the cheese melts and the bread is crisp and flattened, cut diagonally and serve hot.

key-lime-pie.d: A tangy pie made with the juice of small key limes from the Florida Keys, mixed with sweetened condensed milk to thicken without complex cooking, on a Graham cracker crust, a typical dessert of the tropical archipelago.
s: Blitz the Graham crackers into fine crumbs, mix with melted butter and press into a pie pan.
Bake the crust 10 minutes at 180°C, let cool.
Whisk the sweetened condensed milk with the egg yolks and key lime juice until thick and smooth.
Pour onto the cooled crust, bake 15 minutes at 160°C until barely set.
Let cool then chill at least 3 hours, serve with whipped cream.

sonoran-hot-dog.d: A sausage wrapped in bacon and grilled until crisp, nestled in a soft bolillo-style bun and covered with pinto beans, onion, tomato and a creamy jalapeño sauce, a speciality born on the Mexican border.
s: Wrap each sausage in a slice of bacon in a tight spiral.
Grill over medium heat, turning regularly, until the bacon is crisp, about 10 minutes.
Warm the pinto beans, roughly mashed.
Blend jalapeño and mayonnaise for the creamy spicy sauce.
Fill the warm bun with beans, bacon-wrapped sausage, diced onion and tomato, finish with a drizzle of jalapeño sauce.

fish-tacos-baja.d: White fish battered in beer then fried crisp, rolled in a warm corn tortilla with finely shredded cabbage and a creamy spicy sauce, a dish born from cross-border fishing between San Diego and Mexican Baja California.
s: Mix flour and cold beer into a light, foamy batter.
Cut the fish into strips, dip in the beer batter.
Fry in hot oil at 180°C until golden and crisp, drain on paper towel.
Blend mayonnaise and chipotle for the creamy spicy sauce.
Fill the warm tortillas with shredded cabbage, fried fish and chipotle sauce, drizzle with a splash of lime.

cioppino.d: A stew of assorted fish and shellfish in a tomato and white wine broth, born from Fisherman's Wharf's Italian immigrant fishermen who pooled the day's unsold catch into one big shared pot.
s: Sweat sliced onion and garlic in olive oil until translucent.
Add crushed tomato and white wine, simmer 15 minutes into a fragrant base.
Add the fish broth, bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the fish in chunks first, then crab, shrimp, mussels and clams according to their cooking time.
Simmer 12 minutes until all the shellfish have opened, serve scalding with crusty bread.

wisconsin-cheese-curds.d: Small squeaky curds of fresh cheese, battered then fried until forming a golden crust that traps a molten interior, a Wisconsin county fair speciality from America's leading dairy state.
s: Take the cheese curds out of the fridge 20 minutes before breading so they reach room temperature.
Prepare three plates: flour, egg beaten with milk, breadcrumbs seasoned with paprika.
Dredge each curd in flour then egg then breadcrumbs, pressing well to adhere.
Fry in hot oil at 190°C in small batches, only 1 to 2 minutes until golden without letting the cheese fully melt.
Drain on paper towel and serve immediately, piping hot, the cheese should still squeak.

minnesota-hotdish.d: A comforting bake of ground beef, green beans and canned mushroom soup, topped with crispy onion crisps, a church-potluck dish typical of the Scandinavian-American culture of the Midwest.
s: Fry the ground beef with sliced onion until well browned.
Arrange the cooked beef at the bottom of a large oven dish.
Cover with green beans then mushroom soup spread evenly.
Add potato in thin rounds or mashed on top, scatter with grated cheese.
Bake 30 minutes at 190°C, crown with crispy onion crisps for the last 10 minutes.

detroit-coney-dog.d: A sausage drowned under bean-free beef chili, mustard and finely chopped raw onion, born from a century-old rivalry between two neighbouring downtown Detroit restaurants run by Greek and Macedonian immigrants.
s: Fry the beef very finely until almost powder-like, without letting it crisp.
Add tomato paste, cumin and chili powder, moisten lightly and simmer 20 minutes into a thick, bean-free chili.
Poach or grill the sausages until hot.
Place each sausage in a bun, cover generously with hot beef chili.
Finish with a squiggle of mustard and finely chopped raw onion, serve immediately with a fork.

beignets-nola.d: Squares of yeasted dough fried until puffing into golden pillows, buried under a thick snow of powdered sugar, a French dessert turned New Orleans institution, traditionally eaten with chicory coffee and milk.
s: Dissolve the yeast in warm milk, let foam 10 minutes.
Knead with flour, egg, sugar, melted butter and salt into a supple dough, let rise 1 hour.
Roll the dough 1 cm thick, cut into even squares about 8 cm.
Fry in hot oil at 180°C until well puffed and golden on both sides.
Drain and immediately cover with a thick layer of powdered sugar, serve hot.

shoofly-pie.d: An extremely sweet molasses pie topped with a flour-and-butter crumble, a legacy of Pennsylvania's Amish and Mennonite communities, whose name allegedly comes from the flies that had to be shooed from the pie cooling on the windowsill.
s: Mix flour, brown sugar and cold butter with fingertips into a coarse crumble.
Dissolve the molasses, baking soda and egg in hot water until smooth.
Line a pie pan with shortcrust pastry, pour half the crumble into the bottom.
Pour the molasses mixture over the top, cover with the remaining crumble.
Bake 35 minutes at 190°C until the centre barely wobbles, let cool before serving.

peach-cobbler-georgia.d: Ripe, juicy peaches from the state nicknamed the Peach State, simmered with sugar and cinnamon under a biscuit dough that puffs while baking into an irregular golden lid, a late-summer dessert served warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
s: Peel and slice the peaches, mix with half the sugar and cinnamon, let macerate 15 minutes.
Arrange the peaches and their juice in a buttered baking dish.
Mix flour, remaining sugar, baking powder, melted butter, milk and vanilla into a thick biscuit batter.
Pour the batter over the peaches without spreading it completely, leaving some fruit exposed.
Bake 40 minutes at 190°C until golden and bubbling, serve warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

king-crab-alaska.d: Enormous king crab legs from Alaska's icy waters, already precooked at sea on factory ships right after capture, simply reheated by steaming and served with melted butter, a catch among the most dangerous in the world.
s: Take the already precooked king crab legs out of the freezer to thaw slightly.
Heat a large pot of water with a steamer basket.
Steam the legs 8 to 10 minutes until heated through.
Melt the butter with crushed garlic and a little lemon juice.
Crack the shells with a nutcracker, serve with the warm garlic butter and lemon wedges.

tourtiere.d: A pie of minced pork spiced with cinnamon and clove, enclosed in a golden shortcrust pastry, an essential Christmas Eve dish in Quebec, passed down through generations since New France.
s: Fry the minced pork with onion and garlic until well browned.
Add grated potato, cinnamon and clove, moisten with broth.
Simmer covered 25 minutes until thickened and the potato has melted into the filling.
Line a pie pan with shortcrust pastry, fill with cooled filling, cover with a second pastry disc, sealing the edges.
Bake 40 minutes at 190°C until golden, serve hot with homemade fruit ketchup.

soupe-aux-pois-quebec.d: A thick soup of split yellow peas simmered for hours with salt pork, so hearty it earned French Canadians the mocking nickname "pea-soupers" from their English-speaking neighbours.
s: Soak the split peas overnight, drain.
Cook the salt pork in a large volume of water 30 minutes, skim.
Add split peas, onion studded with cloves, carrot and bay leaf.
Simmer covered 2h30 over low heat, stirring occasionally, until the peas break down into a thick soup.
Remove the onion and bay leaf, shred the pork into the soup, serve scalding with homestyle bread.

donair-halifax.d: Spiced beef in the style of Greek kebab, thinly sliced and rolled in pita bread, but topped with a unique sweet sauce of condensed milk, vinegar and garlic — a local invention so beloved it became the city's official dish.
s: Mix the ground beef with garlic powder, oregano and spices, press firmly into a loaf pan to form a compact meatloaf.
Bake 1 hour at 180°C until quite firm, let cool then slice very thin.
Fry the slices in a pan or under the grill until crispy at the edges.
Prepare the sauce by mixing condensed milk, white vinegar and crushed garlic until thick and smooth.
Fill the warm pita with meat, tomato and onion, coat generously with the sweet sauce.

pei-mussels.d: Blue mussels raised on suspended ropes in the island's cold, clean waters, opened in minutes with white wine steam, shallot and cream, the island alone producing the majority of Canada's farmed mussels.
s: Scrape and debeard the mussels thoroughly, discard any that remain open.
Sweat sliced shallot and garlic in butter until translucent.
Add the white wine, bring to a boil.
Add the mussels, cover and cook 6 minutes, shaking the pan, until all have opened.
Add the cream, let thicken 1 minute, scatter with parsley and serve immediately with crusty bread.

jiggs-dinner.d: Salt beef boiled with cabbage, turnip, carrot and potato, traditionally served on Sundays alongside a pease pudding cooked separately in a cloth bag, Newfoundland's most emblematic Sunday meal.
s: Desalt the salt beef overnight, changing the water several times.
Soak the split peas separately overnight, tie them into a cloth bag.
Cook the beef in a large volume of water with bay leaf 2 hours, plunge the pea bag into the same broth.
Add turnip and carrot, cook 30 minutes, then cabbage and potato for the last 20 minutes.
Drain the pea bag, mash into a purée, serve the sliced beef with the vegetables and pea purée on the side.

fish-and-brewis.d: Salt cod and hard bread soaked separately overnight then combined and topped with scrunchions, sizzling fried pork fat cracklings, a Newfoundland fisherman's subsistence dish turned into a Sunday staple.
s: Soak the salt cod and hard bread separately in cold water overnight, changing the water once.
Poach the soaked cod 15 minutes until tender, drain and flake.
Cook the soaked bread in simmering water 10 minutes until softened, drain.
Fry the diced pork fat until crisp with sliced onion, reserve the scrunchions and their fat.
Mix cod and bread in a dish, drizzle with the hot pork fat and crispy scrunchions, serve immediately.

peameal-bacon-sandwich.d: A thick slice of boneless pork loin brined then rolled in yellow cornmeal, pan-fried until golden, served in a soft roll — a sandwich born at Toronto's St. Lawrence Market, sold at dawn to market workers.
s: Brine the pork loin in salt, sugar and water 24 hours chilled.
Rinse and dry, cut into thick slices about 2 cm.
Roll each slice in yellow cornmeal, pressing well to adhere.
Brown the slices in butter over medium heat, 4 minutes per side until well cooked.
Fill a soft mustard-spread roll with one or two slices, serve hot.

butter-tarts.d: Small tartlets filled with brown sugar, butter and maple syrup filling that bubbles while baking until gooey at the centre and lightly crisp on top, a national debate over raisins that has never found consensus.
s: Line small tartlet moulds with shortcrust pastry cut into circles.
Scatter a few raisins in the bottom of each shell for those who like them.
Melt the butter with brown sugar and maple syrup until smooth, let cool slightly.
Stir in the beaten eggs and vanilla, pour the filling two-thirds up each shell.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes at 200°C until the filling bubbles and the edges are golden, let cool before unmoulding.

saskatoon-berry-pie.d: A pie filled with purple berries from the Canadian prairies, similar to blueberries but with a flavour closer to almond, wild-picked along the riverbanks that gave the city its name, between two buttery shortcrust layers.
s: Mix the berries with sugar, flour, lemon juice and a pinch of cinnamon.
Line a pie pan with shortcrust pastry, pour in the berry filling.
Scatter with small pieces of butter.
Cover with a second pastry disc, pinch the edges and cut a few slits to let steam escape.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes at 200°C until golden and bubbling, let cool before slicing.

perogies-canadian.d: Large potato and cheddar dumplings inherited from the Prairie's Ukrainian immigrants, poached then browned in butter with caramelised onions, served with a spoonful of ice-cold sour cream.
s: Knead flour, egg, part of the sour cream and warm water into a supple dough, let rest 30 minutes.
